aggressive_definition: Aggressive incident prostate cancer was defined as regional or distant stage or Gleason score at least 7.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: The study included 692 incident prostate cancer cases, diagnosed 1 to 8 years after study entry, including 270 aggressive cases, with regional or distant stage (n = 90) or Gleason score >or=7 (n = 235), and 844 randomly selected, matched controls.
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The study included 692 incident prostate cancer cases, diagnosed 1 to 8 years after study entry, including 270 aggressive cases, with regional or distant stage (n = 90) or Gleason score >or=7 (n = 235), and 844 randomly selected, matched controls.
reason: Prediagnostic serum carotenoids were evaluated in relation to incident total prostate cancer and an explicitly defined aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: beta-Carotene was associated with an increased risk of aggressive prostate cancer (OR, 1.67; 95% CI, 1.03-2.72 for highest versus lowest quintile; P for trend, 0.13); in particular, regional or distant stage disease (OR, 3.16; 95% CI, 1.37-7.31 for highest versus lowest quintile; P for trend, 0.02); other carotenoids were not associated with risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied OR of 1.67 is explicitly reported for aggressive prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: No association was observed between serum lycopene and total prostate cancer [odds ratios (OR), 1.14; 95% confidence intervals (95% CI), 0.82-1.58 for highest versus lowest quintile; P for trend, 0.28] or aggressive prostate cancer (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.62-1.57 for highest versus lowest quintile; P for trend, 0.433).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied OR of 1.14 is explicitly the total prostate cancer estimate; the separate aggressive estimate is 0.99.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: We investigated the association between prediagnostic serum carotenoids (lycopene, alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, beta-cryptoxanthin, lutein, and zeaxanthin) and risk of prostate cancer in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial, a multicenter study designed to examine methods of early detection and risk factors for cancer.
